source-coverage: Thirty-six source documents are two distinct modalities. Nineteen of20audio recordings have Bashar context; the one Ashtar-attributed creator episode is a singleton. This is not a balanced sample of mediums or civilizations. Token counts use the common analytical tokenizer, not acquisition receipt word definitions.
audio-cosine: Cosine resemblance of20complete unverified ASR documents in a shared audio-only TF-IDF fit, ordered by the exploratory KMeans labels. Diagonal values are self-similarity. Short IDs join sources.json; resemblance is not semantic agreement, independent origin or a speaker comparison.
source-overlay: Two-component TruncatedSVD is fitted only to20audio-source TF-IDF rows. The16publisher texts are projected using that same vocabulary/IDF and SVD. Marker shape indicates modality; colors denote source context/claimed labels. Label callouts reduce overlap without changing point positions. Author, format, length and modality confounding prohibit civilization-level separation claims.
audio-topics: NMF is fit to the20audio document vectors. Three display topics were selected prospectively for readable exploration; candidates2–6and seed-matched stability remain available. Weights sum to1per document. Top-term labels describe model components, not validated themes or distinct belief systems.
theme-overlay: Overlapping predeclared keyword-family rates per1000common tokens, averaged equally across source documents within each labeled context. Counts are dictionary matches, not validated semantic coding. Source-attributed labels and modality are visible; singleton rows have no group-level uncertainty estimate. Promotion/footers and ASR error remain possible contributors.
document-network: Undirected union of each audio document’s two nearest TF-IDF neighbors with cosine≥0.20. Nodes are publication documents, sized by analytical token count; circular positions are purely schematic. Edges encode lexical resemblance, not social relations or independently shared ET knowledge. Threshold sensitivity is exported.
civilization-mentions: Nodes are explicit claimed-civilization/star-system dictionary families and labels give documents with at least one match. Edge labels give documents mentioning both families once per pair; audio and publisher-text panels remain separate. Zero-hit families are omitted from the drawing and retained in the complete count table. Positions are schematic. Star-system/Orion mentions can concern astronomy or fiction; ASR variants are not fuzzy-corrected. Bashar and Ashtar entity names are recorded separately and are not silently mapped to a civilization.
model-diagnostics: NMF reconstruction decreases with model complexity and is not evidence that additional topics are substantively real. Topic stability is seed-matched term-vector cosine; KMeans selection exposes all candidate silhouettes. Neither stability nor a selected partition validates a medium or civilization ontology.
audio-time-profiles: Segments are assigned by their midpoint to ten equal decoded-audio-time bins. Each bin’s keyword occurrences are divided by its own common-token denominator; curves are equal-document means. The Ashtar curve represents one recording, not an estimated population trajectory. Bins are dependent and not independent observations; source intro/outro/advertising remains unsegmented.
